title: The Agent Loop — ReAct with a Step Limit

content.goal: Add a second tool so the agent has a real choice to make.
content.why: An agent proves itself when it must pick the right tool and sometimes chain tools. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 6-7.)
content.verify: The file saves. ATLAS now has two distinct tools — few and distinct, as the theory advises.

content.goal: Write the agent loop with a hard step limit. Add run_agent() to atlas.py.
content.why: The loop is what makes an agent an agent — but without a step cap, a confused agent spins forever. The cap is the first of the three safeguards. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 7, section 7.3.)
content.code:
def run_agent(user_goal, max_steps=6):
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content":
         "You are ATLAS. Think, then use tools when they help. "
         "Do not guess facts you can compute with a tool. "
         "When you have enough to answer, give a final answer and stop."},
        {"role": "user", "content": user_goal},
    ]
    for step in range(max_steps):
        resp = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=MODEL, messages=messages, tools=TOOLS, temperature=0,
        )
        msg = resp.choices[0].message
        if not msg.tool_calls:
            return msg.content              # STOPPING CONDITION: a final answer
        messages.append(msg)
        for tc in msg.tool_calls:
            result = run_tool_call(tc)
            messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id,
                             "content": json.dumps(result)})
    return "Stopped: reached the step limit without finishing."
content.verify: The file saves. The loop's only two outcomes each turn are exactly the theory's: the model wants a tool (run it, loop again) or it is done (stop).

content.goal: Run a task that needs two tools in sequence.
content.why: This exercises the loop across multiple rounds — the thing a single tool cycle could not do. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 7, section 7.1.)
content.verify: ATLAS calls reverse_text, sees the result, calls get_word_count on it, then answers — a genuine multi-step run. The final answer reflects tools run in order, not a guess.
content.troubleshoot: If it answers without using tools, strengthen the system prompt ("do not guess; use the tools") and keep temperature at 0. If it loops, your step limit safely stops it — read the returned message.

content.goal: Add a clearer stopping instruction and a repeated-call guard.
content.why: Ambiguity about stopping is a top failure mode; detecting an identical repeated call breaks accidental loops early. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 7, sections 7.3-7.4.)

content.goal: CHECKPOINT — you have a working single agent (ReAct).
content.why: This is the milestone of Phase 10's first arc: a real agent loop on your machine.
content.verify: All true — ATLAS loops, picks tools, chains them, and stops on a final answer; a step limit prevents runaway loops; a repeated-call guard breaks accidental loops; you can see the trajectory in the trace. You now have AGENT = LLM + TOOLS + LOOP + GOAL, running locally. Next unit hardens it against tool failures.
